speaker: Patient
text: I have these painless, purple-red blisters on both my wrists and hands. The pain is specifically in my left wrist, which is swollen, red, and extremely tender when I try to move it. speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of IV drug use, or have you recently had any invasive procedures or infections? I also need to know if you've experienced any joint pain in other areas or had recent travel to tropical regions.

speaker: Patient
text: No, I don't use drugs or have had any procedures, but I did have pain in my left knee last week that went away on its own. I recently went camping in Minnesota, though I haven't traveled to any tropical places.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice any tick bites while camping in Minnesota, and have you had a rash on your torso or neck? I also need to know if you have experienced any headache, stiff neck, or facial weakness recently.

speaker: Patient
text: I didn't see any tick bites, and I don't have a rash on my torso or neck. I also don't have a headache, stiff neck, or facial weakness, just the chills and malaise I mentioned earlier.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of your recent camping trip in Minnesota, the migratory joint pain, and the distinctive purple-red blistering lesions on your extremities is highly suggestive of a tick-borne illness like Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever, even without the classic central rash. REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture_and_Spot_Fever_Group_Antibody_Test

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal test results rule out Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever, so I need to reconsider the diagnosis. Given the painful, red, swollen wrist and the specific appearance of the lesions, could these blisters be related to a skin infection or a different type of arthropod bite?

speaker: Patient
text: I haven't noticed any other bites, and the blisters on my hands and wrists don't hurt at all. I just feel really sick with chills, and my left wrist is the only joint that's currently painful and swollen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Let me examine the wrist directly to check for warmth and range of motion, and I need to ask if you have had any recent seafood consumption or gastrointestinal symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: The wrist is definitely warm to the touch, and I can barely move it because it hurts so much. I haven't eaten any seafood or had any stomach issues recently, just the chills and body aches.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the wrist is warm and severely tender, I need to rule out septic arthritis or gout. Can you tell me if you have a history of gout, and have you noticed any similar blisters on your feet or lower legs?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I have never had gout before. I haven't noticed any similar blisters on my feet or lower legs, just the ones on my hands and wrists.

speaker: Doctor
text: Let me examine the lesions more closely to see if they are hemorrhagic or vesicular, and have you noticed any bleeding gums or nosebleeds recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I haven't had any bleeding gums or nosebleeds. The lesions look like small, purple blisters, but they are completely painless and don't bleed when touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the painless purpuric lesions on the extremities, fever, and acute monoarthritis after camping, I am concerned for a tick-borne rickettsial infection like Southern Tick-Associated Rash Illness or a similar spotted fever group that may have yielded false negatives early on. REQUEST TEST: Joint_Aspiration_and_Crystal_Analysis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Joint Aspiration (Left Wrist): WBC >50,000 /μL (markedly elevated); Gram Stain: Gram-negative diplococci seen

speaker: Doctor
text:
The joint aspiration confirms septic arthritis caused by Gram-negative diplococci, which is highly characteristic of Neisseria meningitidis. Given the fever, petechial/purpuric lesions, and monoarthritis, I am diagnosing meningococcemia with septic arthritis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Meningococcemia with septic arthritis
